summary: SSE resume sends overlapping token window -> client receives repeated prefix + JSON schema errors
description:
Issue summary:
Customer (NoteAble Analytics) reports that when their SSE streaming connection is interrupted and they reconnect using the Last-Event-ID based resume flow, the resumed stream includes an overlapping prefix of tokens. The overlap results in duplicated text at the consumer layer and, in some cases, schema validation failures when the consumer tries to assemble the full JSON payload (double-curly braces, truncated JSON fragments).

Impact:
- Affects a single dedicated tenant in us-west (NoteAble Analytics).
- Users see duplicated prefixes in generated outputs causing downstream pipelines to fail (JSON parse errors, duplicate IDs).
- Customer is on Dedicated tier and uses a heavily stateful consumer that assumes exact resume boundaries.

Symptoms observed by customer:
- On reconnect, first 12-18 tokens of resumed stream repeat the tail of the previous session.
- Client logs show Last-Event-ID set to the final event id from the first session; server returns resume stream but does not emit a clear resume-boundary marker.
- Consumer fails intermittent JSON schema checks and drops requests.

Why this is high priority:
- P1 / Sev1: production customer with dedicated SLA experiencing data correctness issues (not just display truncation).

Environment details:
- Customer network: corporate NAT + external load balancer in front of client.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a streaming chat request via SSE (python requests/eventsource client) to the Redwood hosted endpoint using the customer's API key.
2) Allow the stream to return ~120 tokens, then forcibly drop the TCP connection (e.g., kill client process or send RST from client-side test harness).
3) Immediately reconnect using Last-Event-ID header set to the 'id' of the last event received. Observe resumed stream entries.
4) Compare token sequence: note duplication of the last 10-20 tokens from previous session and misaligned JSON element boundaries in the assembled payload.
logs: client-tail.log: [2026-03-12T14:11:03Z] received event id=evt-20345 payload="...were likely to "
server-sse.log: [2026-03-12T14:11:09Z] resume request for evt-20345 tenant=noteable dedupe_hint=none
server-servruntime.log: [2026-03-12T14:11:09Z] resumed shard 7: emitting chunk ids evt-20345..evt-20378 (note: start id equals last-event-id)
investigation_notes: Initial triage (Aisha): reproduced locally using a python SSE harness with our public endpoint and a dedicated account. Observed overlap consistent with customer report.

Hypothesis 1 (Jorge): server resume logic emits from the event id inclusive (start==last-event-id) rather than exclusive (start==last-event-id+1), causing a repeated event. This interacts badly with clients that dedupe only on event IDs at a message boundary, not on partial tokens inside an event payload.

Hypothesis 2 (Infra): an upstream proxy (customer LB or our api-gateway) may have reassembled chunks differently on reconnect, causing the last event to be resent without a resume boundary marker.
  Evidence: api-gateway logs show a resume request forwarded but no explicit resume_boundary metadata returned.
Corollary: some clients rely on token-level offsets (server-sent metadata header x-resume-offset) which we do not currently expose; mismatch leads to client-side byte/char duplication.

Reproduction notes: when we force the server to include an explicit 'resume_boundary' event (internal test toggle), clients resumed without duplication. This suggests the server can produce a non-overlapping resume when boundary metadata is present.

Related: SUP-4721 and SUP-11420 captured similar streaming anomalies but those were about chunk truncation and reconnect bucketization; this issue is specific to inclusive resume-start behavior and lack of resume metadata.
Customer impact assessment: high for this tenant because their consumers perform strict JSON validation on concatenated stream segments and do not tolerate token overlap.
comments: 2026-03-12T15:05:00Z - Aisha Malik (Support): Thank you for the report. I've started reproducing this with a local harness and escalated to infra on-call. Please attach a minimal reproduce script if possible.

2026-03-12T15:40:22Z - Jorge Alvarez (SRE): Confirmed reproduction. Hypothesis: inclusive resume start. I can push a guard in sse-handler to make resume start exclusive as a patch for the tenant; need approval to hotfix.
2026-03-12T16:02:10Z - Customer (NoteAble SRE): We can accept a short maintenance window and test a hotfix. This issue is blocking several batch jobs.

2026-03-12T17:30:00Z - Jorge Alvarez (SRE): Drafted PR to send an explicit 'resume_boundary' control event on resume and make resume-start exclusive. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/3456
2026-03-13T09:12:18Z - Aisha Malik (Support): Noted. Scheduling canary with customer for 2026-03-13 21:00 UTC if engineering approves rollout plan.
workarounds: Client-side: implement deduplication at token granularity or ignore the first N tokens after resume if they match recent history (not ideal).
Client-side short term: on reconnect, request a fresh stream (no resume) and re-play last N tokens from server-provided checkpoint APIs instead of SSE resume.

Server-side temporary: gate a tenant-scoped hotfix to change resume semantics to exclusive start and emit a 'resume_boundary' control event on resume. This was tested in dev and avoids duplication in our harness.
resolution: (in progress) Engineering prepared a canary patch that makes resume start exclusive and injects a resume_boundary event with resume_offset + a checksum. Canary scheduled 2026-03-13 21:00 UTC for NoteAble tenant only. If canary succeeds, plan is to roll the fix to dedicated fleet and add an integration test that simulates TCP resets and verifies no token overlap. Follow-ups: add explicit resume metadata to API docs and add monitoring alert for resume_overlap_rate.
next_steps: 1) Execute tenant-scoped canary patch (Jorge) at scheduled time and observe customer test harness results.
2) If canary looks good, merge PR and roll to dedicated fleet during low-traffic window.
3) Create a unit + e2e test for resume boundary cases and add to CI gating for sse-handler changes.
4) Update developer docs and public API doc (Streaming resume section) to include resume_boundary semantics and recommended client-side dedupe guidance.
5) Post-mortem within 5 business days with timeline and decision log.
